headline: Study uses failure composition to choose between agent harness changes and weight training
summary: A new arXiv preprint compares self-evolving an LLM agent's runtime harness with training model weights on the harness-produced trajectories. The authors report that on 72 held-out DeepPlanning tasks, harness evolution raised the composite score for Qwen3.5-4B from 0.156 to 0.292 and for Qwen3.5-9B from 0.305 to 0.390, with four-rollout means. In their diagnosis, process failures such as loops and failed delivery fell while poor delivered plans remained; trajectory-trained LoRA adapters reportedly transferred gains to the base harness and reduced content failures for the 9B model. The authors also report a +0.09 gain on 117 unseen WebArena-Lite tasks, where the harness exposed two pages of history rather than one and adapters did not add to that gain. These are paper-reported outcomes from a bounded benchmark study, not independently reproduced results or evidence that the intervention rule generalizes to all agents or tasks.
